newsitem.title: CANADA: WCE canola ends up as commercials, commissions buy.
newsitem.headline: WCE canola ends up as commercials, commissions buy.

text.p: WCE canola ended up as commercial firms and commission houses bought and on active spreading, traders said.

"RBC-DS and Cargill bought July, 400 July-Nov spread and there were November hedges at the close," a trader said. July WCE futures crush profit margin fell to -10.06 Thursday from -9.22 Wednesday. May-July spread $6.50, July-Nov $44, Aug-Nov $41. Volume was 4,825 lots, or 96,500 tonnes, with 465 hedges.
Japan bought 3,000-4,000 tonnes overnight, sources said.
July canola up $1.50 to $424, November down $0.60 at $379.70. July flax rose $1.30 to $343.50 on commercial demand to cover old exports, November up $1.90 to $332.80. Volume 340.

Feed wheat drew underlying support came from growing concern about flooding in southern Manitoba and expectations the Canadian Wheat Board will raise its world price outlook at 1400 CDT Thursday, traders said.
July feed wheat rose $0.50 to $172, December lost $0.20 to $170. Alberta Wheat Pool bought deferreds, traders said.
May western barley fell $0.10 to $140.60 and October lost $0.40 to $140.10 as hedges met commission buying. Volume 700.
RBC-DS bought five May feed peas contracts unchanged at US$217, October lost US$0.90 at US$197.50 on commercial sales.
(All prices in Canadian dollars/tonne except oats, peas).
